check-import-scope's rust_Imported_Names (language-kernels/programming/rust/rustlang/rust_import_scope.go) double-counts a use-with-alias: it walks the whole use-declaration subtree and appends the use_as_clause's alias (the real bound name, ChangeSource) but ALSO independently appends the inner scoped_identifier's last path segment (Source, the pre-alias name) since that scoped_identifier's parent is the use_as_clause rather than another scoped_identifier, so the walker's skip condition never fires for it. Source is never actually bound into scope by 'pub use source::Source as ChangeSource;' -- only ChangeSource is -- but the checker treats the discarded path segment as a second countable import name, then finds its only textual match at line 85's unrelated '.Source()' method call (a method defined on WorkspaceChangeSet in workspace/change_set.rs, spelled the same by coincidence) inside Test_A_Change_Set_Should_Carry_Its_Source_And_Its_Changes, and reports that as the import's sole use. ChangeSource itself (the actual imported/bound name) is used throughout this file and re-exported from crate::lib.rs for the whole workspace (nomos_workspace::ChangeSource), so the suggested remedy of moving the pub use into that one test function is not applicable: it is a public re-export the whole crate and its dependents need, not a module-scope convenience import serving one function.
